sections.sectionSummaryBrief: These three matters correspond to wisdom, repentance, and good deeds, representing son, servant, and the will of Atzmus.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that these three matters are the three matters of wisdom, repentance, and good deeds.
Wisdom
(Torah)
is the matter of a son
(as above in section 5),
repentance, whose matter is that a person goes out and is nullified from his self-existence
(as above in section 2),
is analogous to the matter of accepting the yoke,
a servant,
and good deeds are the mitzvos themselves,
the will of Atzmus.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Through repentance, deeds become good and luminous, for the drawing of Atzmus is primarily in mitzvos, requiring the nullification of repentance.

translations.translation: And this can be connected with the well-known explanation34
of the phrase "repentance and good deeds,"
that through repentance the deeds
(the deeds of the mitzvos)
become good deeds and luminous35,
for the drawing of Atzmus is
(primarily)
in the fulfillment of the mitzvos
(deeds),
and not in the nullification of repentance
(and acceptance of the yoke).
But in order that the deeds be good deeds and luminous,
that the drawing of Atzmus within them be revealed,
this is through the nullification of repentance and acceptance of the yoke.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Even in Torah study, the nullification of a servant is necessary, as one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times differs from one who reviews it one hundred times.

translations.translation: Now, although the matter of engaging in Torah is that a person's existence
(his understanding and comprehension)
be in accordance with the Torah,
nevertheless,
even in the study of Torah there must be the nullification of a servant,
the yoke of Torah36.
And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said37
that one who reviews his chapter one hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times,
because in this extra time he changes his nature and habit38,
for even in Torah there must be the nullification of a servant39.
